rv.q: This is a pitch-perfect production of an astonishingly fine new play and it must surely have an extended life beyond the cramped confines of the Theatre Upstairs.
Michael Longhurst’s surefooted production is both entertaining and deeply moving.
The result is a brain-teasing 70-minute play that packs an enormous amount in, but also one that, to achieve an emotional climax, undermines its own scientific principles.

Eventually, the evening is expertly drawn together so that without noticing viewers who were originally nonplussed and then amused find themselves affected in a very different fashion by a really subtle and insightful piece of writing.
Longhurst’s surefooted production is both entertaining and deeply moving.

cn.t: Critics largely praise *Constellations* for its ingenious structure and emotional depth, though some find it undermines its own logic. Nick Payne's multiverse love story packs big ideas into 70 minutes—mostly to stunning effect.
